set.title: 300 Real-Life Conversations
set.about: Maya moves to a new city and learns to live there: neighbors, trains, doctors, work, friends, and then the beaches, mountains and markets. Short conversations, in thirty places, with the phrases you really need.
set.author: NoaLingua

maya.name: Maya
maya.about: Maya has just moved to the city for a new job. She is curious and polite, she is learning the language, and she asks a lot of questions.

leon.name: Leon
leon.about: Leon lives across the hall from Maya. He is warm and talkative, he loves to cook, and he knows every corner of the city.

timo.name: Timo
timo.about: Timo is Leon's son. He is seven, he is full of questions, and he never stands still.

greta.name: Greta
greta.about: Greta owns Maya's building and lives on the ground floor. She is kind but strict, and she remembers everything.

nora.name: Nora
nora.about: Nora works with Maya. She is organized and direct, and she always has a plan.

yuki.name: Yuki
yuki.about: Yuki is in Maya's language class. She is quiet at first and funny once you know her, and she never goes anywhere without her camera.

omar.name: Omar
omar.about: Omar is Maya's old friend, visiting for a few weeks. He is relaxed and always hungry, and he keeps losing things.

conversations.title: Introducing yourself to someone for the first time.
conversations.scene: Maya meets a man on the stairs of her new building.

lines.text: Hi! Are you new in the building?
Yes, I just moved in. I'm Maya.
Nice to meet you, Maya. I'm Leon.
Nice to meet you too.
Where are you from?
I'm from Canada. And you?
I'm from here. I live across the hall.
Great! See you around, Leon.

conversations.title: Meeting a new neighbor and starting a conversation.
conversations.scene: Maya meets Greta, the owner of her building, at the front door.

lines.text: Good morning! You must be the new tenant.
Yes, good morning. I'm Maya.
I'm Greta. I live on the ground floor.
Nice to meet you, Greta. Is this your garden?
Yes, I grow tomatoes and herbs.
It's beautiful.
Thank you. If you need anything, just knock.
Thank you, that's very kind.

conversations.title: Making small talk with a stranger while waiting in line.
conversations.scene: Maya waits in a long line at the bakery on Saturday morning.

lines.text: This line is really long today.
Yes! Is it always like this on Saturdays?
Usually. Their bread is the best in town.
That's why I'm here. What do you recommend?
Try the rye bread. It's still warm at this time.
Thanks, I will. Lovely weather today, isn't it?
Yes, finally some sun!
Oh, it's my turn. Have a nice day!

conversations.title: Introducing two people to each other.
conversations.scene: Maya is walking with Yuki when they meet Leon.

lines.text: Hi, Maya! How are you?
Fine, thanks. Leon, this is my friend Yuki.
Hello, Leon. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too, Yuki.
Yuki, Leon is my neighbor.
Oh, from across the hall?
That's right. How do you two know each other?
We're in the same language class.

conversations.title: Asking someone to repeat or speak more slowly.
conversations.scene: Greta tells Maya about the trash cans, but she speaks very fast.

lines.text: The trash goes out on Tuesday night, the paper on Thursday.
Sorry, could you speak more slowly, please?
Of course. The trash goes out on Tuesday.
Tuesday. Could you repeat the second part?
The paper goes out on Thursday.
Paper on Thursday. Did I get that right?
Yes, exactly.
Thank you for your patience.

conversations.title: Explaining that you're learning the local language.
conversations.scene: Maya buys apples at the market and tries to speak the language.

lines.text: Good morning! What can I get you?
A kilo of apples, please.
You have a nice accent. Where are you from?
I'm from Canada. I'm learning the language.
You speak very well!
Thank you, but I'm still a beginner. Please speak slowly.
No problem. That's 3 euros.
Here you are. Thank you!

conversations.title: Giving someone a compliment and responding to one.
conversations.scene: Before class, Maya looks at Yuki's new photos.

lines.text: Yuki, your photos are amazing!
Really? Thank you, that's so nice of you.
Where did you take this one?
By the river, at sunset.
You have a real talent.
You're too kind. And I love your scarf!
Thanks! It was a present from my mom.
The color really suits you.

conversations.title: Apologizing after accidentally bumping into someone.
conversations.scene: Maya is looking at her phone and walks into a man with a coffee.

lines.text: Ouch! Careful!
I'm so sorry! Are you OK?
Yes, I'm fine. Don't worry.
I wasn't looking. Sorry about your coffee.
It's just a little on my sleeve.
Let me buy you another one.
That's kind, but it's really no problem.
Sorry again. Have a good day!

conversations.title: Politely interrupting someone to ask a question.
conversations.scene: Nora is talking with a colleague when Maya needs a quick answer.

lines.text: So the meeting moves to Friday.
Friday is fine for me.
Sorry to interrupt. Can I ask a quick question?
Of course, Maya. What is it?
Where can I find paper for the printer?
In the cupboard next to the window.
Thanks. Sorry again for interrupting.
No problem at all.

conversations.title: Ending a conversation naturally and saying goodbye.
conversations.scene: Maya and Leon chat on the stairs, but Maya has to go.

lines.text: And that's the best pizza place in town.
Great, I'll try it this week.
Order the one with mushrooms.
I will. Well, I should go now. I'm meeting a friend.
Of course. It was nice talking to you.
You too! Thanks for the tip.
Any time. See you around!
See you, Leon. Bye!

conversations.title: Asking a stranger for directions to a specific address.
conversations.scene: Maya is looking for a dentist's office at Park Street 14.

lines.text: Excuse me, how do I get to Park Street 14?
Park Street? Go straight on to the traffic lights.
Straight on to the lights. And then?
Then turn left. Number 14 is on the right.
Is it far from here?
No, about five minutes on foot.
Thank you very much!
You're welcome.

conversations.title: Finding the nearest public restroom.
conversations.scene: Omar has had two coffees and needs a restroom, fast.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a public restroom near here?
Yes, in the park behind the church.
Is it free?
It costs 50 cents. Do you have coins?
No, only a card.
Then try the mall across the street. It's free there.
Great, thanks a lot!

conversations.title: Asking how far away a place is and how long it takes to get there.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to walk to the castle on the hill.

lines.text: Excuse me, how far is the castle from here?
About two kilometers.
How long does it take on foot?
Around twenty-five minutes. It's uphill.
And by bus?
Ten minutes. Take bus number 7.
Thanks! I think I'll walk.
Good idea. The view is great.

conversations.title: Understanding directions involving streets, turns, and landmarks.
conversations.scene: Omar asks the way to the museum and tries to remember every turn.

lines.text: Excuse me, which way is the city museum?
Go along this street until you see a big church.
Until the church. OK.
Turn right there, then take the second street on the left.
Right at the church, then the second left?
Exactly. Then cross the bridge. The museum is opposite the park.
Cross the bridge, opposite the park. Got it!
You can't miss it. It's a yellow building.

conversations.title: Asking someone to show you a location on a map.
conversations.scene: Maya has a paper map, but she can't find the flower market.

lines.text: Sorry, could you show me on the map?
Sure. Where do you want to go?
To the flower market.
Let me see. We're here, next to the station.
Ah, I see.
And the market is here, by the river.
Can you mark it with my pen?
Of course. There you go.
Thank you so much!

conversations.title: Explaining that you're lost and need help.
conversations.scene: Omar's phone is dead, and he has no idea where he is.

lines.text: Excuse me, can you help me? I'm lost.
Of course. Where do you want to go?
To my friend's apartment. It's on Linden Street.
Linden Street is quite far. Do you know the number?
Number 22. My phone is dead, so I can't check the map.
Take tram 3 over there. Get off at the fourth stop.
Tram 3, the fourth stop. Thank you so much!
Good luck!

conversations.title: Finding an ATM, pharmacy, or supermarket nearby.
conversations.scene: Maya needs cash, some aspirin and milk.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there an ATM near here?
Yes, at the bank on the corner.
And a pharmacy?
There's one next to the bank, with a green cross.
Great. Is there also a supermarket nearby?
Yes, but it's a bit further. Two streets down, on the left.
Is it open now?
Yes, until 10 tonight.
Thanks a lot!

conversations.title: Asking whether a neighborhood is safe to walk through at night.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to walk back from a concert late at night.

lines.text: Is it safe to walk through the old town at night?
Yes, it's generally very safe. There are lots of people.
What about the area near the station?
It's OK, but some streets are quite dark.
Would you take a taxi?
After midnight, yes. Or take the night bus.
Where does the night bus stop?
Right in front of the hotel.
Perfect, thank you.

conversations.title: Finding an alternative route when a street is closed.
conversations.scene: Maya is walking to work, but the street is closed for a market.

lines.text: Excuse me, why is the street closed?
There's a street market today, until 6.
I need to get to the post office. Is there another way?
Yes. Take the next street on the right and go around.
Is it much longer?
Only about five minutes more.
OK. So right, and then left again?
Exactly. Then you're back on the main street.
Thank you, officer.

conversations.title: Asking where the nearest elevator, escalator, or accessible entrance is.
conversations.scene: Maya is shopping with Greta, who can't take the stairs today.

lines.text: My knee hurts. I can't take these stairs today.
Excuse me, where is the nearest elevator?
The elevators are at the back, next to the café.
Is there also an escalator?
Yes, but it's not working today, sorry.
And is there an accessible entrance on this side?
Yes, the side door has a ramp. I can open it for you.
Thank you, young man. That's very kind.

conversations.title: Buying a train ticket at the ticket counter.
conversations.scene: Maya buys a ticket for the train to Belmar, a town on the coast.

lines.text: Hello. A ticket to Belmar, please.
One way or round trip?
Round trip, please. I'm coming back on Sunday.
First or second class?
Second class. How much is it?
34 euros. Do you have a discount card?
No, I don't.
Then it's 34 euros. Card or cash?
Card, please.

conversations.title: Asking about train departure and arrival times.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to know about the trains to Belmar.

lines.text: When is the next train to Belmar?
At 10:15, from platform 4.
And what time does it arrive?
Is there a later one?
Yes, every two hours. The next one is at 12:15.
Is it direct?
The 10:15 is direct. The 12:15 has a change.
OK, I'll take the 10:15. Thanks!

conversations.title: Finding the correct platform for your train.
conversations.scene: The board shows two trains to Belmar, and Maya and Omar are confused.

lines.text: Look, there are two trains to Belmar.
Which platform is ours? Let me ask.
Excuse me, is this the platform for the 10:15 to Belmar?
No, that's platform 4, over there.
How do we get there?
Take the underpass and go up the stairs on the left.
Do we have time?
Yes, it leaves in eight minutes.
Thanks! Come on, Omar.

conversations.title: Understanding announcements about delays or cancellations.
conversations.scene: An announcement comes over the speakers, but it is hard to hear.

lines.text: The 10:15 train to Belmar is delayed by approximately 20 minutes.
What did it say? Is our train canceled?
No, it's delayed. About twenty minutes, I think.
Let's ask to be sure.
Excuse me, how long is the delay?
Twenty minutes for now. Please listen for updates.
We apologize for the inconvenience.
Well, time for a coffee then.

conversations.title: Asking whether you need to change trains.
conversations.scene: The conductor checks Maya's ticket, and she asks about her route.

lines.text: Tickets, please.
Here you are. Do I need to change trains?
Yes, in Calden. Change to the regional train.
How much time do I have in Calden?
Twelve minutes. The train leaves from the same platform.
Is it easy to find?
Yes, just stay on platform 2.
Great, thank you.

conversations.title: Finding your carriage and reserved seat.
conversations.scene: Omar finds a woman sitting in his reserved seat.

lines.text: Excuse me, I think this is my seat.
Really? Which seat do you have?
Car 7, seat 45. By the window.
Oh, this is car 6. Car 7 is the next one.
Oh no, sorry! My mistake.
No problem. It happens all the time.
Is car 7 this way?
Yes, through that door.

conversations.title: Asking about ticket validation and travel passes.
conversations.scene: Yuki has a paper ticket and is not sure what to do with it.

lines.text: Do I need to validate this ticket?
Yes, use the yellow machine on the platform before you get on.
What happens if I forget?
The inspector can give you a fine.
I see. Is there a travel pass for a week?
Yes, the weekly pass costs 25 euros. It's for all regional trains.
Do I validate that one too?
Only once, on the first day.
Great, I'll take one.

conversations.title: Finding out where to store your luggage.
conversations.scene: Omar has a big suitcase and three hours before his train.

lines.text: Is there somewhere to leave luggage here?
Yes, there are lockers downstairs.
How much are they?
5 euros for small lockers, 8 for large ones.
My suitcase is quite big.
Then take a large one. You pay by card at the machine.
How long can I leave it?
Up to 24 hours.
Perfect. Thanks!

conversations.title: Missing a connecting train and asking for alternatives.
conversations.scene: Maya's first train was late, and she has missed her connection in Calden.

lines.text: Hi. My train was late, and I missed my connection.
Where are you going?
To Belmar. The train left five minutes ago.
The next one is in an hour. Your ticket is still valid.
Is there a faster option?
There's a bus at 14:20, but you need a new ticket.
How long does the bus take?
About the same. I'd wait for the train.
OK. Can you write a note on my ticket?
Of course. Here's a stamp, just in case.

conversations.title: Reporting a lost item at the train station.
conversations.scene: Omar left his jacket on the train. Of course he did.

lines.text: Hello. I left my jacket on the train.
Which train, and when?
The 10:15 from the city. It arrived an hour ago.
What does the jacket look like?
It's dark blue, with a phone charger in the pocket.
Let me check. No, nothing yet, sorry.
Can I leave my phone number?
Yes. Fill in this form, and we'll call you.
Thank you. I lose everything!

conversations.title: Finding the correct bus or subway line.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to get to the university by subway.

lines.text: Excuse me, which line goes to the university?
The green line. Line 2.
In which direction?
Direction North Park. It's four stops.
And where is the green line?
Down the stairs, then follow the green signs.
Thank you!
You're welcome.

conversations.title: Asking where to buy a public transportation ticket.
conversations.scene: Maya is at a bus stop, and she has no ticket.

lines.text: Excuse me, where can I buy a bus ticket?
At the machine over there, or in the app.
Can I pay the driver?
No, not anymore. Only the machine or the app.
Does the machine take cards?
Yes, cards and coins.
How much is a single ticket?
2 euros. It's valid for 90 minutes.
Thanks for your help!

conversations.title: Asking the bus driver whether the bus stops at your destination.
conversations.scene: Greta gets on a bus she doesn't usually take.

lines.text: Does this bus stop at the hospital?
Yes, it does. It's the sixth stop.
Can you tell me when we get there?
Sure. You can also see the stops on the screen.
My eyes are not so good anymore.
No problem. I'll call it out for you.
Thank you, that's very kind.
Please take a seat.

conversations.title: Understanding how to validate a ticket.
conversations.scene: Omar gets on the tram with a paper ticket in his hand.

lines.text: Excuse me, what do I do with this ticket?
You need to validate it. Use the orange machine by the door.
How does it work?
Put the ticket in with the arrow first.
Like this?
Yes. Wait for the beep. Now it shows the time.
Is it valid for the whole trip?
For 90 minutes, on all trams and buses.
Great. Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking which stop to get off at.
conversations.scene: Maya is going to a concert hall she has never been to.

lines.text: Excuse me, which stop is best for the concert hall?
Get off at Opera Square.
Is that far?
No, three more stops.
Is the concert hall close to the stop?
Yes, it's right across the street.
Great. How will I know it's Opera Square?
There's a screen at the front. And I'm getting off there too.
Perfect. I'll follow you!

conversations.title: Finding out how to transfer between different lines.
conversations.scene: Yuki needs to get from the blue line to the red line.

lines.text: Excuse me, how do I get to Central Market?
Take the blue line to Freedom Square, then change to the red line.
Do I need a new ticket to change lines?
No, your ticket is valid for the whole trip.
How do I find the red line at Freedom Square?
Follow the red signs. It's a short walk underground.
Which direction should I take on the red line?
Direction Airport. Central Market is the second stop.
Thank you so much!

conversations.title: Asking someone to move so you can get off.
conversations.scene: The bus is full, and Omar's stop is next.

lines.text: Excuse me, I'm getting off at the next stop.
Sorry, I can't move. It's so full.
Could you just step back a little?
Let me try. Is that better?
Yes, thanks. Excuse me, can I get through?
Careful, there's a bag on the floor.
Got it. Thank you, sorry!

conversations.title: Offering your seat to an elderly person or someone who needs it.
conversations.scene: An old man with a walking stick gets on the metro.

lines.text: Excuse me, would you like to sit down?
Oh, thank you, but I'm fine.
Please, take my seat. I'm getting off soon.
Are you sure?
Yes, of course.
That's very kind of you, young lady.
You're welcome. Be careful, the train is moving.
Thank you. People are so friendly here.

conversations.title: Finding transportation late at night.
conversations.scene: Maya and Yuki leave a party after midnight, and the metro has stopped.

lines.text: The metro closed at midnight. How do we get home?
Is there a night bus?
Yes, the N3, but only every hour.
Let me ask that bus driver.
Excuse me, does the N3 go to the city center?
Yes, but the next one is at 1:30.
That's 45 minutes. Should we take a taxi?
Let's share one. It's cheaper for two.

conversations.title: Dealing with a ticket inspection or an incorrect ticket.
conversations.scene: An inspector checks tickets, and Omar's ticket is for the wrong zone.

lines.text: Tickets, please.
Here you are.
This ticket is only for zone A. We're in zone B now.
Oh, I didn't know. I'm a tourist. I'm sorry.
I understand, but without a valid ticket, the fine is 60 euros.
Is there anything I can do? It was an honest mistake.
This time, you can buy a zone B ticket from me for 3 euros.
Thank you so much. I'll buy one.
Next time, check the zones before you travel.

conversations.title: Checking in for an international flight.
conversations.scene: Maya checks in for a work trip abroad.

lines.text: Good morning. Your passport, please.
Here you are.
Do you have any bags to check in?
Yes, just this suitcase.
Please put it on the belt. Window or aisle?
A window seat, please.
Here's your boarding pass. Boarding starts at 9:40, gate B12.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking about baggage allowance and overweight luggage.
conversations.scene: Nora's suitcase is full of samples for a meeting.

lines.text: Your suitcase is 26 kilos. The limit is 23.
How much does it cost for the extra weight?
It's 50 euros for an overweight bag.
That's a lot. What is the allowance for hand luggage?
One bag up to 8 kilos, plus a small handbag.
Can I move some things into my hand luggage?
Yes, of course.
OK. Give me a minute to repack.
No problem. Put it back on the scale when you're ready.

conversations.title: Going through airport security.
conversations.scene: Maya puts her things in the trays at the security check.

lines.text: Please put your bag and jacket in the tray.
Do I need to take out my laptop?
Yes, laptops and liquids in a separate tray.
Is this bottle of water OK?
No, sorry. Liquids only up to 100 milliliters.
Oh, I'll drink it now then.
Please walk through. Arms up, please.
Is everything OK?
Yes, you can take your things. Have a good flight.

conversations.title: Answering questions at passport control.
conversations.scene: Nora lands abroad and waits at passport control.

lines.text: Good evening. Passport, please.
Here you are.
What's the purpose of your visit?
Business. I have meetings with a client.
How long are you staying?
Four days. I fly back on Friday.
Where are you staying?
At the Grand Hotel, in the city center.
Thank you. Enjoy your stay.

conversations.title: Finding your departure gate.
conversations.scene: Maya's boarding pass says gate B12, but she can only see A gates.

lines.text: Excuse me, where is gate B12?
Go straight, past the shops, then follow the signs for B.
Is it far?
About ten minutes on foot.
Boarding starts at 9:40. Do I have time?
Yes, it's 9:15 now. But don't stop for shopping!
I'll try. Thanks!

conversations.title: Understanding a gate change or flight delay.
conversations.scene: Maya and Nora wait at the gate when an announcement starts.

lines.text: Attention, please. Flight 274 now departs from gate C3.
Did they say C3? That's our flight!
Yes. Our gate has changed.
Departure is delayed by 40 minutes.
Delayed too? We'll miss the start of the meeting.
Let's go to C3 and ask about the new time.
Good idea. I'll send an email to the client.
Don't worry, Nora. We still have time.

conversations.title: Asking airport staff for help when you miss your flight.
conversations.scene: Omar's bus was stuck in traffic, and his plane has just left.

lines.text: Hi. I've just missed my flight. What can I do?
Let me see your booking. You were on the 11:20 flight.
Yes, the bus got stuck in traffic. Is there another flight today?
There's one at 18:05, but there's a change fee of 80 euros.
Is there anything cheaper? Maybe a flight tomorrow morning?
Tomorrow at 7:30, the fee is only 30 euros.
Can you also put me on the waiting list for an earlier flight?
Yes, but there's no guarantee. Stay close to the gate.
OK, I'll take tomorrow's flight, and the waiting list too.
Done. Here is your new boarding pass.

conversations.title: Reporting missing or damaged luggage.
conversations.scene: Omar waits at the belt, but his suitcase never comes.

lines.text: Hello. My suitcase didn't arrive.
I'm sorry. Can I see your baggage tag?
Here it is. It's a black suitcase with a red ribbon.
Thank you. It's still at your departure airport.
When will it get here?
Tomorrow afternoon. We can deliver it to your hotel.
Yes, please. And the handle of my other bag is broken.
Then please fill in this damage form too.
Of course. This trip is going great.

conversations.title: Answering questions at customs.
conversations.scene: A customs officer stops Nora and her suitcase of samples.

lines.text: Excuse me. Anything to declare?
No, nothing to declare.
What's in this suitcase?
Product samples for a business meeting.
Are they for sale?
No, they're free samples. I have a letter from my company.
Can I see it, please?
Of course. Here it is.
That's fine. You can go.

conversations.title: Rebooking a canceled flight.
conversations.scene: On the way home, Maya and Nora's flight is canceled because of a storm.

lines.text: Our flight was canceled. Can you rebook us, please?
Of course. I'm sorry for the trouble. Let me look.
We need to be home by tomorrow evening.
There's a flight tomorrow at 13:10, with one stop.
Is there a direct flight?
The direct flight is full, I'm afraid.
Then we'll take the one with the stop. Will you pay for a hotel tonight?
Yes. Here are two hotel vouchers and two vouchers for dinner.
Thank you. Will our bags go straight to the final destination?
Yes, they're checked through.

conversations.title: Calling a taxi and explaining your pickup location.
conversations.scene: Maya calls for a taxi to the airport early in the morning.

lines.text: City Taxi, good morning.
Hello. I need a taxi to the airport, please.
When do you need it?
Tomorrow at 5 in the morning.
What's the pickup address?
Linden Street 22. It's the building next to the pharmacy.
And your name?
Maya.
OK, Maya. The driver will call you when he arrives.

conversations.title: Telling the driver your destination.
conversations.scene: Omar gets into a taxi at the station.

lines.text: Hello! Where to?
To the Hotel Riva, please. It's near the old harbor.
The Hotel Riva? On Harbor Street?
Yes, that's the one. Here's the address.
OK. It's about fifteen minutes.
Can you put my suitcase in the trunk?
Of course. Get in, I'll do it.

conversations.title: Asking how much the ride will cost.
conversations.scene: Before she gets in, Yuki wants to know the price.

lines.text: How much is it to the university?
About 15 euros.
Do you use the meter?
Yes, always.
Can I pay by card?
Yes, card or cash.
Is there an extra charge for my bag?
No, the bag is free.
OK, let's go.

conversations.title: Asking the driver to take a different route.
conversations.scene: Maya's taxi is stuck in traffic, and she has a meeting in twenty minutes.

lines.text: Wow, the traffic is really bad.
Yes, there's an accident on the main road.
Could you take a different route? I'm in a hurry.
We can go along the river. It's longer, but faster now.
Let's do that, please.
OK. It may cost two or three euros more.
That's fine. I just need to be there by 10.
Don't worry, we'll make it.

conversations.title: Explaining where to stop and drop you off.
conversations.scene: Greta takes a taxi home with heavy shopping bags.

lines.text: We're on your street. Which number?
Number 8. The blue door on the left.
Here?
A bit further, please. Stop just after the tree.
Like this?
Perfect. You can stop here.
Shall I help you with the bags?
Oh, yes, please. You're very kind.

conversations.title: Paying for a taxi and requesting a receipt.
conversations.scene: Nora arrives at a meeting and needs a receipt for work.

lines.text: Here we are. That's 23.50 euros.
Can I pay by card?
Sure. Here's the card machine.
Could I have a receipt, please? It's for work.
Of course. Do you want the company name on it?
Yes, please. It's Altis Design.
Here you are. Have a good day.
Thanks, you too.

conversations.title: Reporting something you forgot in a taxi.
conversations.scene: Omar's phone isn't in his pocket, so he calls the taxi company from the hotel.

lines.text: City Taxi, how can I help?
Hello. I left my phone in one of your taxis.
When was your ride?
About an hour ago, from the station to the Hotel Riva.
Do you remember anything about the car?
It was a white car. The driver had a big beard.
Let me call the drivers. Can I have a number to call you back?
Please call the Hotel Riva, room 304.
Good news! The driver found it. He'll bring it to your hotel.
Thank you so much! Today is my lucky day.

conversations.title: Renting a car and understanding the rental agreement.
conversations.scene: Leon rents a car for a weekend trip with Maya and Omar.

lines.text: Here's the agreement. Please read it before you sign.
Is insurance included in the price?
Basic insurance, yes. But the deductible is 1,000 euros.
What does that mean exactly?
If there's any damage, you pay the first 1,000 euros.
Can I reduce that?
With full insurance, you pay nothing. It's 15 euros a day more.
OK, I'll take full insurance. Do I return it with a full tank?
Yes, or we charge for the fuel. Is there a second driver?
No, just me. Where do I return the keys?
Here, at this desk, by 6 on Sunday.

conversations.title: Asking for help at a gas station or electric charging station.
conversations.scene: Leon's rental car is electric, and he has never charged one.

lines.text: Excuse me, can you help me? I don't know how to charge this car.
Sure. First, open the charging flap here.
Got it. And now?
Plug the cable in, then hold your card on the screen.
How long does it take to charge?
About 40 minutes to 80 percent.
And how much does it cost?
Around 20 euros. There's a café inside while you wait.
Perfect. Thanks for your help!

conversations.title: Dealing with a car breakdown and calling roadside assistance.
conversations.scene: Leon's car stops on a country road, and he calls roadside assistance.

lines.text: Roadside assistance, how can I help you?
Hi. My car has broken down. It stopped and won't start again.
Are you in a safe place?
Yes, I'm on the side of the road, with the hazard lights on.
Where exactly are you?
On the road to Valdora, about five kilometers after the village.
Can you see a sign or a kilometer marker?
Yes, there's a sign. Kilometer 14.
OK. A mechanic will be there in about 45 minutes.
Thanks. Should I wait in the car?
Wait behind the safety barrier, and put on your safety vest.

conversations.title: Booking a hotel room by phone.
conversations.scene: Maya calls the Hotel Riva in Belmar to book a room for the weekend.

lines.text: Hotel Riva, good afternoon.
Hello. I'd like to book a room for this weekend.
For how many nights?
Two nights, Friday and Saturday.
A single or a double room?
A double, please. Is breakfast included?
Yes. It's 120 euros per night with breakfast.
That's fine. Do you have a room with a sea view?
Yes, for 20 euros more.
Perfect, I'll take it.

conversations.title: Checking in at hotel reception.
conversations.scene: Maya arrives at the Hotel Riva on Friday evening.

lines.text: Good evening. I have a reservation. My name is Maya.
Welcome! Can I see your ID, please?
Here you are.
Thank you. Two nights, a double room with a sea view.
Yes, that's right.
Your room is 304, on the third floor.
What time is checkout?
At 11. Here's your key card. Enjoy your stay!

conversations.title: Asking about breakfast, Wi-Fi, and hotel facilities.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to know everything about the hotel.

lines.text: What time is breakfast?
From 7 to 10, in the restaurant on the ground floor.
And what's the Wi-Fi password?
It's on your key card holder.
Is there a gym or a pool?
There's a small gym, but no pool. The beach is close.
Can I leave my bags here after checkout?
Yes, we can keep them for you.
Great, thanks.

conversations.title: Reporting a problem with your room.
conversations.scene: Maya's room is cold, and the shower has no hot water.

lines.text: Reception, how can I help?
Hi, this is room 304. There's no hot water in the shower.
Oh, I'm sorry. Is the water completely cold?
Yes. And the heating isn't working either.
I'll send someone from maintenance right away.
How long will it take?
About ten minutes. Can I offer you a drink in the bar while you wait?
That would be nice, thank you.

conversations.title: Requesting a quieter or different room.
conversations.scene: Omar's room is above the bar, and the music is loud.

lines.text: Excuse me, could I change rooms? Mine is very noisy.
I'm sorry. Which room are you in?
Room 112, right above the bar.
Ah, yes. The music goes on until midnight.
Do you have a quieter room, maybe on a higher floor?
Let me check. Yes, room 508 is free. It faces the garden.
Is it the same price?
Yes, the same price. Here's your new key.
Thank you, that's much better.

conversations.title: Asking for extra towels, pillows, or blankets.
conversations.scene: Maya meets a housekeeper in the hallway.

lines.text: Excuse me, could I have two more towels, please?
Of course. Bath towels or small ones?
Bath towels, please. And an extra pillow?
No problem. Do you need a blanket too?
Yes, please. It's a bit cold at night.
I'll bring everything to your room. Which number?
304. Thank you so much.
You're welcome. Five minutes.

conversations.title: Asking hotel staff for local recommendations.
conversations.scene: Omar has one free evening in Belmar.

lines.text: Can you recommend a good place for dinner?
Do you like seafood? Try Lumo, by the harbor.
Is it expensive?
Not too bad. Around 30 euros per person.
Is there anything to do in the evening?
There's live music on the main square on Fridays.
Today is Friday! How do I get there?
It's a ten-minute walk. Here, I'll show you on the map.
Thanks, that's very helpful.

conversations.title: Extending your stay for another night.
conversations.scene: Maya loves Belmar and wants to stay longer.

lines.text: Hi. Could I stay one more night?
Let me check. Yes, your room is free tomorrow too.
Great! Is it the same price?
On Sunday it's cheaper: 100 euros with breakfast.
Perfect. So I check out on Monday?
Yes, on Monday at 11.
Can I pay for everything then?
Of course. I'll add it to your bill.

conversations.title: Losing your room key and requesting a replacement.
conversations.scene: Omar comes back late, and his key card is gone.

lines.text: Hi. I'm so sorry, I lost my key card.
No problem. What's your room number?
508. My name is Omar.
Can I see some ID, please?
Here's my passport.
Thank you. Here's a new card. The old one won't work anymore.
Is there a charge for that?
No, it's free. But please don't lose this one!
I'll try my best.

conversations.title: Checking out and questioning an unexpected charge.
conversations.scene: At checkout, Maya sees something on her bill she doesn't understand.

lines.text: I'd like to check out, please. Room 304.
Of course. Here's your bill.
Sorry, what is this charge of 18 euros?
That's the minibar. Two drinks and some chocolate.
But I didn't use the minibar at all.
Let me check. Oh, you're right, it was another room. I'm so sorry.
No problem. And the city tax, is that per night?
Yes, 2 euros per person per night. It's the law here.
OK, that makes sense. Can I pay by card?
Of course. Thank you for staying with us.

conversations.title: Reserving a restaurant table.
conversations.scene: Leon calls a restaurant to book a table for Maya's birthday.

lines.text: Nala Bistro, good evening.
Hello. I'd like to reserve a table for Saturday.
For how many people?
For four, at 8 o'clock.
Let me see. Yes, that's fine. What name, please?
Leon. It's a birthday. Could we have a quiet table?
Of course. A table by the window.
Perfect. Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking for a table without a reservation.
conversations.scene: Omar and Maya walk into a busy restaurant without a booking.

lines.text: Hi. Do you have a table for two?
Do you have a reservation?
No, we don't.
Then you'll need to wait about twenty minutes.
Can we sit outside?
Yes, there's one free table on the terrace.
Great, we'll take it.
Follow me, please.

conversations.title: Understanding the menu and asking about unfamiliar dishes.
conversations.scene: Maya reads the menu and doesn't know half of the dishes.

lines.text: Excuse me, what's this dish here?
It's a local stew with beef, onions and red wine.
Is it spicy?
No, not at all. It's quite mild.
What does it come with?
With potatoes or fresh bread.
Sounds good. And what's the soup of the day?
Pumpkin soup with ginger.
I'll try the stew, with bread.

conversations.title: Asking about ingredients because of food allergies.
conversations.scene: Yuki is allergic to nuts, so she checks every dish.

lines.text: Excuse me, I'm allergic to nuts. Does this salad have nuts?
Yes, it has walnuts. But we can make it without them.
Thank you. And the pesto pasta?
The pesto has pine nuts, I'm afraid.
It's a serious allergy. Can the kitchen be careful?
Of course. I'll tell the chef. Would you like the menu with allergy information?
Yes, please. That would help a lot.
Here you are. The dishes with nuts have a small symbol.

conversations.title: Ordering food and drinks.
conversations.scene: Omar is very hungry and ready to order.

lines.text: Are you ready to order?
Yes. I'd like the chicken with rice, please.
And to drink?
A large water and a lemonade, please.
Still or sparkling water?
Sparkling. And can I have some bread first?
Of course. Anything else?
Maybe a dessert later. I'm very hungry!

conversations.title: Requesting changes to a dish.
conversations.scene: Nora likes the burger, but not everything in it.

lines.text: Could I have the burger without onions, please?
Of course.
And could I have salad instead of fries?
Yes, no problem. Any dressing?
The dressing on the side, please.
And how would you like the meat?
Medium, please.
Got it. No onions, salad instead of fries, dressing on the side.
Perfect, thank you.

conversations.title: Asking the waiter for something you need during the meal.
conversations.scene: Leon is having lunch with his son Timo, who has just spilled his juice.

lines.text: Dad, I spilled my juice!
Oh no. Excuse me!
Yes?
Could we have some napkins, please?
Of course. Here you are.
And could we have another glass of apple juice?
And a spoon for my ice cream!
Timo, ask nicely.
Can I have a spoon, please?
Of course you can!

conversations.title: Complaining politely about incorrect or poorly prepared food.
conversations.scene: Omar's steak is not what he asked for.

lines.text: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.
Yes, is everything OK?
Not really. I asked for my steak medium, but it's very well done.
Oh, I'm sorry. Let me take it back to the kitchen.
Thank you. And the fries are cold, I'm afraid.
I'm really sorry. We'll bring you a new plate right away.
Thank you. No hurry.
And your drinks are on the house today.
That's very kind. Thank you.

conversations.title: Asking for the bill and splitting the payment.
conversations.scene: Maya and Leon finish dinner and want to pay.

lines.text: Excuse me, could we have the bill, please?
Of course. Here you are.
Let me get this one.
No, Leon, let's split it.
Can we pay separately?
Sure. Who had what?
I had the fish and a beer.
So that's 24 euros for you, and 19 for the lady.
I'll pay by card. Is service included?
No, but tips are always welcome!

conversations.title: Ordering takeaway food or asking to pack leftovers.
conversations.scene: Omar can't finish his pizza, and he wants something for later.

lines.text: Excuse me, could I take the rest home?
Of course. I'll put it in a box for you.
Thank you. And can I order a pizza to take away?
Sure. Which one?
The vegetarian one, please. How long will it take?
About fifteen minutes.
Great. It's for my friend Maya.
Lucky friend! I'll bring it with your bill.

conversations.title: Finding a particular product in a supermarket.
conversations.scene: Maya can't find the rice in the big supermarket.

lines.text: Excuse me, where can I find rice?
In aisle 5, next to the pasta.
Thank you. And do you sell coconut milk?
Yes, in the international aisle, at the end.
Is it on the left or on the right?
On the right, on the bottom shelf.
Great. And where are the eggs?
Next to the milk.

conversations.title: Asking the price of fruit or vegetables at a market.
conversations.scene: Leon buys vegetables for dinner at the Saturday market.

lines.text: How much are the tomatoes?
3 euros a kilo.
And the peppers?
50 cents each, or three for 1 euro.
I'll take a kilo of tomatoes and three peppers.
Anything else?
Some fresh basil, please.
Here you go. That's 4.50 euros altogether.
Here you are. Thanks!

conversations.title: Buying meat or cheese by weight.
conversations.scene: Greta is buying cheese and ham for the weekend.

lines.text: I'd like 200 grams of this cheese, please.
This one? The mountain cheese?
Yes. Could you slice it thinly?
Of course. It's a little over, 220 grams. Is that OK?
That's fine.
And 150 grams of ham, please.
Cooked or smoked?
Smoked, please.
Anything else?
No, that's everything, thank you.

conversations.title: Asking whether a product is fresh, local, or organic.
conversations.scene: Maya wants good strawberries for a cake.

lines.text: Are these strawberries local?
Yes, from a farm ten kilometers away.
Are they organic?
Yes, they're certified organic. Here's the label.
When were they picked?
This morning. They're very fresh.
Can I try one?
Of course. Go ahead.
Delicious! I'll take two boxes.

conversations.title: Understanding food labels and expiration dates.
conversations.scene: Maya and Yuki read the labels on a yogurt.

lines.text: Maya, what does this date mean?
It says "best before". The yogurt is still OK after it.
And this one says "use by".
That's stricter. Don't eat it after that day.
This yogurt is for tomorrow. Is it OK?
Yes, if you eat it before then.
Does it have sugar? I can't read the small print.
12 grams per 100 grams. That's quite a lot.
Then I'll take the natural one.

conversations.title: Finding an alternative when a product is unavailable.
conversations.scene: Leon needs fresh basil for his sauce, but the shelf is empty.

lines.text: Excuse me, do you have any more fresh basil?
Sorry, we're out of it today.
Will you get more tomorrow?
Yes, the delivery comes in the morning.
I need it for tonight. Is there anything similar?
We have dried basil, or a basil plant in a pot.
A plant is a great idea! Where is it?
In the flower section, by the entrance.
Thanks a lot.

conversations.title: Asking about discounts, loyalty cards, and special offers.
conversations.scene: Greta wants to save money on her shopping.

lines.text: Do you have a loyalty card?
No. What do I get with it?
You get points, and a 10 percent discount every month.
Is it free?
Yes, it's free. Just fill in this form.
Are there any special offers today?
Yes, two for one on coffee.
Oh! Then I'll get another coffee.
Good choice! I'll wait.

conversations.title: Using a self-checkout machine and requesting assistance.
conversations.scene: Omar tries the self-checkout, and the machine keeps beeping.

lines.text: Unexpected item in the bagging area.
What? There's nothing there!
Excuse me, can you help me? The machine has stopped.
Sure. What happened?
I scanned the bananas, but it says there's an unexpected item.
You need to weigh fruit first. Put it on the scale.
Oh, I see. And how do I pay?
Press the green button, then hold your card here.
Thanks. These machines hate me.

conversations.title: Resolving an incorrect price at the checkout.
conversations.scene: Maya notices that the cheese costs more than the shelf said.

lines.text: Excuse me, I think this price is wrong.
Which one?
The cheese. On the shelf it says 2.99, but here it's 3.99.
Let me check. Do you remember where it was?
Yes, in aisle 3, with a yellow discount sign.
My colleague is checking now.
You're right. The offer started today. I'll correct it.
Thank you. Could I have the receipt, please?
Of course. Sorry for the mistake.

conversations.title: Shopping at a local farmers' market and talking to vendors.
conversations.scene: Leon shows Maya his favorite stall at the farmers' market.

lines.text: Maya, this is the best honey in the region.
Leon! Good morning. Is this a friend?
Yes, this is Maya, my neighbor.
Nice to meet you. Do you make the honey yourself?
Yes, we have bees on our farm in the hills.
Which one do you recommend?
The forest honey. It's dark and strong. Try some.
It's delicious! I'll take a jar.
For Leon's friends, it's 6 euros instead of 7.
See? I told you he's the best.

conversations.title: Asking for your clothing or shoe size.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants some sneakers, but there are none in her size on the shelf.

lines.text: Excuse me, do you have these in size 38?
Let me look. In white or in black?
In white, please.
Here you are. Size 38.
They're a bit small. Do you have a 39?
Yes. Try these.
These are perfect. How much are they?
79 euros.
I'll take them.

conversations.title: Trying on clothes and asking where the fitting rooms are.
conversations.scene: Maya has three dresses in her hands.

lines.text: Excuse me, where are the fitting rooms?
At the back, next to the mirrors.
Can I try on three things?
Yes, up to five. Here's a number.
Thank you.
How is it?
The blue one is tight. Is there a medium?
Yes, one moment. I'll bring it.

conversations.title: Asking whether an item is available in another color.
conversations.scene: Omar likes a jacket, but not the color.

lines.text: Do you have this jacket in another color?
Yes, in gray and dark green.
In my size? Large.
Gray in large, yes. Green only in medium.
Can I see the gray one?
Here you are.
Can you order the green one in large?
Yes. It takes about a week.
I'm leaving soon. I'll take the gray one.

conversations.title: Comparing two products before purchasing.
conversations.scene: Maya can't decide between two pairs of headphones.

lines.text: What's the difference between these two headphones?
This pair has better sound. That one is lighter.
Which one has the longer battery?
The black ones. Up to 30 hours.
And which is better for phone calls?
The white ones. They have a better microphone.
Is the price the same?
No. The black ones cost 20 euros more.
I'll take the white ones, then. I make a lot of calls.

conversations.title: Negotiating a price at a market.
conversations.scene: Omar finds an old camera at the flea market.

lines.text: How much is this camera?
60 euros. It's a classic.
It's nice, but it's quite old. Would you take 40?
40? No, it works perfectly. 55.
What about 45? I'm paying cash.
Let's say 50, and I'll give you the case too.
OK, 50 with the case. It's a deal.
Deal! Enjoy it.

conversations.title: Returning an item and requesting a refund.
conversations.scene: Maya wants to return a coffee machine that doesn't work.

lines.text: Hello. I'd like to return this coffee machine.
What's the problem with it?
It doesn't heat the water properly.
Do you have the receipt?
Yes, here it is. I bought it last week.
Can I get a refund?
Yes. Do you want the money back, or a new machine?
The money back, please. To my card.
OK. It can take three to five days.

conversations.title: Exchanging a product for a different size.
conversations.scene: Yuki's new sweater is too big.

lines.text: Hi. Can I exchange this sweater for a smaller size?
Of course. Do you have the receipt?
Yes. I bought it on Saturday.
What size is it?
Large. I need a small.
Let me look. Yes, here's a small in the same color.
Can I try it on first?
Sure. The fitting room is over there.
It fits perfectly. Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking about warranties and repairs for electronics.
conversations.scene: Nora wants to buy a laptop for work, and she asks about the warranty.

lines.text: How long is the warranty on this laptop?
Two years, and you can extend it to four.
What does the extended warranty cover?
Repairs, and also accidents, like a broken screen.
And if it breaks, where do I take it?
You bring it here, and we send it for repair.
How long does a repair usually take?
About two weeks. We can lend you a laptop in the meantime.
OK. I'll take it with the four-year warranty.

conversations.title: Buying a gift and requesting gift wrapping.
conversations.scene: Omar buys a present for Maya, to thank her for everything.

lines.text: I'm looking for a present for a friend.
What does she like?
She loves books and good tea.
How about this tea set? It's very popular.
That's perfect. Could you gift wrap it, please?
Of course. Which paper do you like?
The green one. And can I add a card?
Sure. Here's a pen.

conversations.title: Asking for advice about a souvenir or local product.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants a typical gift to take home to Japan.

lines.text: What is a typical souvenir from this region?
Many people buy olive oil or local wine.
Something small, please. It's for my flight home.
Then try this lavender soap. It's handmade here.
Is it really from this region?
Yes, from a farm in the hills. It says so on the label.
It smells lovely. How much is it?
6 euros, or three for 15.
I'll take three!

conversations.title: Making a doctor's appointment.
conversations.scene: Maya has had a sore throat for days, so she calls a clinic.

lines.text: Good morning, City Clinic.
Hello. I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor, please.
Are you a patient here?
Not yet. I just moved to the city.
Then please bring your ID and your insurance card. What's the problem?
I've had a sore throat and a fever for three days.
The doctor can see you today at 4:30. Is that OK?
Yes, that's perfect. Thank you.

conversations.title: Registering at a clinic and describing the reason for your visit.
conversations.scene: Maya arrives at the clinic for her first visit.

lines.text: Hello. I have an appointment at 4:30. My name is Maya.
Welcome. Is this your first visit?
Yes, it is.
Then please fill in this form. Can I see your insurance card?
Here you are.
What's the reason for your visit today?
I have a sore throat and a fever.
Thank you. Please take a seat. The doctor will call you.

conversations.title: Explaining symptoms and how long you've had them.
conversations.scene: The doctor asks Maya about her symptoms.

lines.text: What seems to be the problem?
I have a sore throat, and I feel very tired.
How long have you had these symptoms?
Since Monday. About four days.
Do you have a fever?
Yes, 38.5 last night.
Any cough or headache?
A little cough, but no headache.
Let me look at your throat. Open your mouth, please.

conversations.title: Describing pain, its location, and severity.
conversations.scene: Omar hurt his back carrying his suitcase.

lines.text: Where does it hurt?
Here, in my lower back, on the left side.
How bad is the pain, from 1 to 10?
About a 7. It's worse when I bend down.
Is it a sharp pain or a dull pain?
Sharp, especially in the morning.
When did it start?
Two days ago, after I lifted a heavy suitcase.
It sounds like a pulled muscle. Rest, and no heavy lifting.

conversations.title: Explaining your medical history, allergies, and medications.
conversations.scene: Nora sees a new doctor for a check-up and answers questions about her health.

lines.text: Do you have any allergies?
Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin.
Thank you, that's important. Are you taking any medication?
I take a tablet for my blood pressure every morning.
Do you know the name and the dose?
Yes, I have it here on my phone.
Have you had any operations or serious illnesses?
I had my appendix removed when I was twelve.
Does anyone in your family have heart problems?
My father has high blood pressure too.

conversations.title: Buying medicine at a pharmacy and understanding dosage instructions.
conversations.scene: Maya picks up her medicine and checks how to take it.

lines.text: Hello. I have a prescription from my doctor.
Thank you. Here's your medicine.
How often should I take it?
One tablet three times a day, after meals.
For how many days?
For seven days. Finish the whole pack, even if you feel better.
Can I drink alcohol with it?
No, better not. And it may make you a little sleepy.
OK. Thank you for explaining.

conversations.title: Visiting a dentist for tooth pain.
conversations.scene: Omar has had a toothache all night and gets an emergency appointment.

lines.text: Hello, Omar. What's the problem?
I have a terrible toothache. Here, at the back.
When did it start?
Yesterday evening. I couldn't sleep.
Does it hurt with hot or cold drinks?
Yes, especially with cold drinks.
Let me see. You have a small hole. I can fix it today.
Will it hurt?
No, I'll give you an injection first. You won't feel anything.
OK. Thank you, doctor.

conversations.title: Having a blood test or medical examination.
conversations.scene: Maya has a blood test before her yearly check-up.

lines.text: Good morning. Are you here for a blood test?
Yes. My doctor sent me.
Did you eat anything this morning?
No, nothing. Only water.
Good. Please roll up your sleeve and make a fist.
I don't like needles.
Look at the window and take a deep breath. Just a small pinch.
Is it done already?
Yes, all done. Press on this for a minute.
When will I get the results?
In two or three days. The doctor will call you.

conversations.title: Calling an ambulance for a medical emergency.
conversations.scene: Greta has fallen on the stairs and can't get up, so Leon calls for help.

lines.text: Emergency services. What is your emergency?
My neighbor fell down the stairs. She can't get up.
Is she conscious and breathing?
Yes, she's awake and breathing, but her leg hurts a lot.
What's the address?
Linden Street 22, the ground floor.
An ambulance is on the way. Don't move her.
OK. Should I give her some water?
No, nothing to eat or drink. Keep her warm and stay with her.
Greta, help is coming. Everything will be OK.
Thank you, Leon.

conversations.title: Asking about medical bills, insurance, and follow-up appointments.
conversations.scene: After her visit, Maya asks about payment and her next appointment.

lines.text: Excuse me, do I need to pay anything today?
Your insurance covers the visit. You only pay 10 euros for the prescription.
Will I get a bill for the blood test?
No, that goes directly to your insurance company.
And if the insurance doesn't pay?
Then we'll send you a letter. But usually there's no problem.
The doctor wants to see me again in two weeks. Can I book that now?
Of course. How about Tuesday the 14th at 9?
That's fine. Could I get a reminder by text message?
Yes, we send one the day before.

conversations.title: Reporting a stolen phone, wallet, or passport to the police.
conversations.scene: Omar's wallet and phone were stolen on the metro.

lines.text: Hello. I want to report a theft. My wallet and phone were stolen.
I'm sorry. When and where did it happen?
About an hour ago, on the metro, on the red line.
Did you see the person?
No. It was very crowded. I only noticed when I got off.
What was in the wallet?
About 80 euros, two bank cards and my driver's license.
Have you blocked your cards yet?
Yes, I called the bank right away. I need a report for my insurance.
Of course. Fill in this form, and I'll give you a copy.

conversations.title: Asking for help when you feel threatened or unsafe.
conversations.scene: A man has been following Yuki for several streets, so she goes into an open café.

lines.text: Excuse me, can you help me? A man is following me.
Oh no. Come in, you're safe here.
He's been behind me for ten minutes. He's outside now.
The one in the gray hoodie? I see him.
Can you call the police, please?
Yes, I'm calling now. Sit here, away from the window.
Thank you. I'm a bit scared.
That's normal. The police will be here soon. Do you want some water?
Yes, please. Can I also call my friend Maya?
Of course. Take your time.

conversations.title: Reporting a fire and following evacuation instructions.
conversations.scene: The fire alarm rings in the middle of the night, and there's smoke in the hallway.

lines.text: Maya! Wake up! There's smoke in the hallway!
What? Is it a fire?
I think so. Don't take the elevator. Use the stairs.
Should I take anything?
Only your phone and your keys. Hurry!
Has anyone called the fire department?
Greta did. Go down and wait outside, across the street.
Is everyone out? Stay together and wait for the firefighters.
Is everyone OK? Where is Timo?
He's here with me. We're all safe.

conversations.title: Witnessing an accident and calling emergency services.
conversations.scene: Maya sees a car hit a cyclist at a crossroads.

lines.text: Emergency services. What's your emergency?
There's been an accident. A car hit a cyclist.
Where are you?
At the corner of Park Street and Market Street.
Is the cyclist injured?
Yes. He's on the ground, and his arm is bleeding.
Is he awake? Can he talk?
Yes, he's talking, but he's in pain.
An ambulance is coming. Don't move him, and stay with him.
OK. The driver has stopped too. He's here.
Good. The police will want to talk to you both.

conversations.title: Explaining what happened after a traffic accident.
conversations.scene: Another car hit the back of Leon's car at a red light. Nobody is hurt.

lines.text: I'm so sorry. Are you OK?
Yes, I'm fine. Are you hurt?
No, I'm OK. I didn't see that the light was red.
Let's move the cars to the side of the road.
Should we call the police?
Nobody is hurt, so let's fill in an accident report together.
OK. Here's my insurance information and my license.
Thanks. I'll take some photos of both cars.
Good idea. The damage isn't too bad, luckily.
Here's my phone number, in case your insurance needs it.

conversations.title: Reporting a missing child or family member.
conversations.scene: At the city festival, Leon suddenly can't see his son Timo.

lines.text: Please help me. I can't find my son!
Stay calm. How old is he, and what does he look like?
He's seven. He has short brown hair, and he's wearing a red jacket.
Where did you last see him?
Next to the carousel, about ten minutes ago.
What's his name?
Timo. He knows my phone number.
I'll tell all my colleagues. Please stay here, by the carousel.
We found him! He was at the ice cream stand.
Dad! I just wanted some ice cream.
Timo! Never walk away like that again.

conversations.title: Asking for help when you're stranded somewhere unfamiliar.
conversations.scene: Yuki and Maya miss the last bus back from a mountain village.

lines.text: The last bus left at 6. What do we do now?
Let's ask someone. Excuse me, can you help us?
Of course. What's wrong?
We missed the last bus to the city. Is there a taxi here?
There's one taxi in the village, but the driver is on vacation.
Is there a train station nearby?
In the next town, five kilometers away. Trains run until 11.
Could you call us a taxi from the next town?
I can do better. My son is driving there now. He can take you.
That's so kind of you! Thank you so much.

conversations.title: Responding to severe weather or a natural disaster warning.
conversations.scene: A severe storm warning comes on the radio, and Greta tells Maya what to do.

lines.text: Maya, did you hear? There's a storm warning for tonight.
No! How serious is it?
Strong winds and heavy rain. Maybe flooding near the river.
What should I do?
Bring your plants and chairs in from the balcony.
OK. Anything else?
Charge your phone, and have a flashlight ready, in case the power goes out.
Should I stay at home?
Yes, don't go out unless you have to. And stay away from the river.
Thank you, Greta. You're always prepared.

conversations.title: Contacting your embassy or consulate for assistance.
conversations.scene: Omar's passport was in his stolen wallet, and he flies home in four days.

lines.text: Embassy, consular section. How can I help?
Hello. My passport was stolen, and I fly home on Friday.
I'm sorry to hear that. Did you report it to the police?
Yes, I have the police report.
Then you can apply for an emergency travel document.
What do I need to bring?
The police report, two passport photos and your flight booking.
How long does it take?
Usually one or two working days. Can you come tomorrow morning?
Yes, I'll be there. Thank you so much.

conversations.title: Explaining an emergency when you don't know the necessary vocabulary.
conversations.scene: Yuki's skin is red and itchy, and she can't find the right words.

lines.text: Hello. I need help, but I don't know the word.
Don't worry. Can you show me?
Here, on my arms. It's red, and it's very... I can't say it.
Does it itch? Like this?
Yes! It itches. Since this morning.
Did you eat something new, or touch a plant?
I ate nuts by mistake. I'm allergic.
Can you breathe normally? Is your throat OK?
Yes, I can breathe.
Good. Take this allergy tablet now. If it gets worse, call 112.

conversations.title: Calling about an apartment advertised for rent.
conversations.scene: Yuki is looking for an apartment, and she calls about an ad.

lines.text: Hello?
Hello. I'm calling about the apartment for rent on Hill Street.
Yes, it's still available.
How big is it?
Two bedrooms, a living room and a small balcony. 65 square meters.
How much is the rent?
850 euros a month, plus utilities.
Can I come and see it?
Of course. Is Thursday at 6 OK?
Yes, perfect. See you then.

conversations.title: Viewing an apartment and asking about its condition.
conversations.scene: Yuki visits the apartment with Maya, who came to help.

lines.text: Here's the living room. It gets a lot of sun.
It's nice. Is the furniture included?
The kitchen is furnished, but the rest is empty.
Does everything in the kitchen work?
Yes, the fridge and the stove are almost new.
What about the windows? They look old.
They're old, but they close well. The heating is new.
Is there any problem with damp or mold?
No, never. You can look anywhere you like.
Is it quiet at night?
Yes, the bedrooms face the courtyard.

conversations.title: Discussing rent, deposits, and the rental agreement.
conversations.scene: Yuki likes the apartment and asks about the contract.

lines.text: I like it. What are the conditions?
The rent is 850 euros, plus about 150 for utilities.
How much is the deposit?
Three months' rent. You get it back when you move out.
How long is the contract?
One year at first. After that, it continues month by month.
What is the notice period if I want to leave?
Three months, in writing.
Are pets allowed?
Small pets, yes. No dogs, I'm afraid.
OK. Can I read the contract at home before I sign?
Of course. Take your time.

conversations.title: Meeting your landlord and collecting the keys.
conversations.scene: Yuki meets the landlord on moving day to collect the keys.

lines.text: Good morning! Here are your keys.
Thank you! What are all these keys for?
The big one is for the front door. The small one is for the mailbox.
And where are the meters?
In the basement. Let's write down the numbers together.
Good idea. Who do I call if something breaks?
Call me first. Here's my number.
And when do I pay the rent?
By the third of every month, by bank transfer.
Perfect. Thank you for everything.

conversations.title: Reporting a leaking pipe or broken appliance.
conversations.scene: There is water on Maya's kitchen floor, and it's coming from under the sink.

lines.text: Greta, sorry to bother you. There's a leak in my kitchen.
Oh no. Where is it coming from?
From the pipe under the sink. There's water everywhere.
Turn off the water. There's a small tap under the sink.
OK, I did it. It's stopped now.
Good. I'll call a plumber right away.
Thank you. Also, the washing machine is making a strange noise.
The washing machine too? I'll ask him to look at both.
Thank you, Greta.

conversations.title: Calling about an electricity, water, or internet outage.
conversations.scene: All the lights in Maya's apartment have gone out.

lines.text: Good evening, City Power. How can I help?
Hello. There's no electricity in my apartment.
What's your address?
Linden Street 22.
Is it only your apartment, or the whole street?
The whole street, I think. All the windows are dark.
Yes, there's a problem in your area. Our team is working on it.
How long will it take?
About two hours. We're sorry for the trouble.
OK. Thanks for the information.

conversations.title: Talking politely to a neighbor about noise.
conversations.scene: Leon's music woke Maya up twice this week.

lines.text: Hi, Leon. Do you have a minute?
Sure, Maya. What's up?
It's a bit awkward. Your music was quite loud last night.
Oh no! Did it wake you up?
Yes, at about 1. And on Tuesday too.
I'm really sorry. I had friends over, and I didn't notice.
No problem. Could you turn it down after 10?
Of course. And next time, just knock on my door.
Thanks for understanding.
Thanks for telling me so nicely.

conversations.title: Understanding and paying utility bills.
conversations.scene: Maya has her first electricity bill and doesn't understand it.

lines.text: Greta, can you help me with this bill?
Of course. Let me see.
Why are there two amounts?
This one is what you used. This one is the monthly advance for next year.
So I pay 60 euros every month from now on?
Exactly. And at the end of the year, they check your meter.
What if I used less?
Then you get money back. If you used more, you pay the difference.
How do I pay it?
The easiest way is a direct debit from your bank account.

conversations.title: Receiving a delivery or collecting a parcel from a neighbor.
conversations.scene: Maya was at work when her parcel came, so Leon took it.

lines.text: Maya! The delivery man left a parcel for you.
Oh, thank you! Did you sign for it?
Yes, I did. Here it is.
It's heavy! It's my new lamp.
Do you need help to carry it?
No, it's OK. Thanks for taking it.
Any time. I'm home most days.
Then I owe you a coffee!

conversations.title: Arranging for a repair technician to visit your home.
conversations.scene: Maya calls a technician because her washing machine is broken.

lines.text: Good morning, Fix Fast. How can I help?
Hello. My washing machine is broken. Can someone come and look at it?
Of course. What's the problem?
It doesn't drain, and it makes a loud noise.
I can come on Wednesday, between 9 and 12. Is that OK?
Can you come later? I work in the mornings.
Then Thursday, between 4 and 6.
Perfect. How much does a visit cost?
40 euros for the visit, plus parts if needed.
OK. See you on Thursday.

conversations.title: Opening a bank account.
conversations.scene: Maya needs a local bank account for her salary.

lines.text: Good morning. I'd like to open a bank account.
Of course. Do you have your passport and proof of address?
Yes, here's my passport and my rental contract.
Thank you. Do you work here?
Yes, I have a work contract with Altis Design.
Would you like a checking account or a savings account?
A checking account, for my salary.
Perfect. Please sign here. Your card will come in the mail in a week.
Can I use online banking from today?
Yes, I'll give you your login details now.

conversations.title: Asking about bank fees, cards, and account conditions.
conversations.scene: Before she signs, Maya asks about the costs.

lines.text: Are there any monthly fees for this account?
It's 5 euros a month, but it's free if your salary comes in.
What about the debit card?
The debit card is free. A credit card costs 30 euros a year.
Can I withdraw money from any ATM?
From our ATMs, yes, for free. Other banks charge about 2 euros.
And can I use the card abroad?
Yes. There's a small fee for payments in other currencies.
OK, the debit card is enough for now.

conversations.title: Reporting a card blocked or retained by an ATM.
conversations.scene: The ATM has kept Omar's card, and the bank is about to close.

lines.text: Excuse me, the ATM outside just kept my card.
I'm sorry. What happened exactly?
I typed my PIN, and then the screen froze. The card didn't come out.
Did you type the wrong PIN more than once?
No, only once, and it was correct.
Then it's a technical problem. Can I see your ID?
Here's my passport.
We'll open the machine tomorrow morning. You can collect your card at 9.
Tomorrow? But I need money tonight.
Do you have another card? There's an ATM at the station too.
Yes, my credit card. OK, I'll come back tomorrow at 9.

conversations.title: Exchanging foreign currency.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to change some money before a trip.

lines.text: Hello. I'd like to change 200 euros into dollars.
Of course. Today the rate is 1.08.
Is there a commission?
Yes, 2 percent. So you get 211 dollars.
Can I have some small bills, please?
Sure. Tens and twenties?
Yes, perfect.
Here you are. Please count it.
That's right. Thank you.

conversations.title: Making a bank transfer and checking transaction details.
conversations.scene: Maya's rent transfer has not arrived, so she calls her bank.

lines.text: Customer service, how can I help?
Hello. I made a transfer on Monday, but it hasn't arrived.
Let me check. Can you give me the amount and the date?
850 euros, on Monday the 3rd, to Greta Weber.
I see it. The transfer is still processing.
Why is it taking so long?
The account number has a mistake. One number is wrong.
Oh no! What can I do?
We'll cancel it and send the money back. Then you can make a new transfer.
Thank you. I'll check the number very carefully this time.

conversations.title: Buying a SIM card and choosing a mobile plan.
conversations.scene: Omar wants a local SIM card for his last two weeks.

lines.text: Hello. I need a SIM card for two weeks.
Do you want a prepaid card or a contract?
Prepaid. What plans do you have?
This one has 20 gigabytes and unlimited calls for 15 euros a month.
Does it work in other countries too?
In the whole EU, yes. Outside the EU, it costs extra.
Great. I'll take it. Do you need my passport?
Yes, we need ID for every SIM card.
Here you are. Can you put it in my phone for me?
Sure. Give me a minute.

conversations.title: Sending a letter or package at the post office.
conversations.scene: Maya sends a birthday package to her mom in Canada.

lines.text: Hello. I'd like to send this package to Canada.
Please put it on the scale. It's 2 kilos.
How much does it cost?
32 euros by standard mail, or 55 by express.
How long does standard mail take?
About two weeks.
Her birthday is in ten days. Express, please.
Please fill in this customs form. What's inside?
A sweater and some chocolate.
OK. Here's your tracking number.

conversations.title: Registering your address at a government office.
conversations.scene: Maya must register her new address at the town hall.

lines.text: Next, please. How can I help?
I'd like to register my address. I moved here last month.
Do you have an appointment?
Yes, at 10:20. My name is Maya.
Thank you. I need your passport and the confirmation from your landlord.
Here's my passport, and here's the letter from my landlady.
Everything is in order. Please sign this form.
Do I get a certificate?
Yes, here it is. Keep it safe. You'll need it for the bank and the tax office.

conversations.title: Filling out official documents and asking for explanations.
conversations.scene: Yuki fills in a form for a residence permit and gets stuck.

lines.text: Excuse me, could you help me with this form?
Of course. Which part?
What does "place of residence" mean? Is it my address here?
Yes, exactly. Your current address in the city.
And here, "marital status"?
That's whether you're single or married.
Single. And do I need to sign every page?
Only the last page, at the bottom.
Should I write in capital letters?
Yes, please, so we can read it easily.

conversations.title: Discussing a problem with an insurance company.
conversations.scene: Omar calls his travel insurance about his stolen phone, and they want more papers.

lines.text: Good afternoon, how can I help you?
Hi. I sent a claim for my stolen phone last week. What's happening with it?
Let me check. Your claim is on hold. We need more documents.
But I sent the police report already.
Yes, we have that. We also need the receipt for the phone.
It was a present. I don't have the receipt.
Then a bank statement or a photo of the box with the serial number can help.
I have a photo of the box. Where should I send it?
By email, with your claim number in the subject.
OK. And how long will it take after that?
Usually two weeks.

conversations.title: Attending a job interview.
conversations.scene: Before she moved to the city, Maya had a job interview at Altis Design.

lines.text: Thank you for coming, Maya. Tell me a little about yourself.
I'm a graphic designer. I have five years of experience in advertising.
Why do you want to work here?
I love your projects, and I want to work with international clients.
What is your biggest strength?
I'm creative, but I'm also good with deadlines.
And a weakness?
Sometimes I spend too long on details. I'm working on it.
Do you have any questions for us?
Yes. What does a typical day look like in this team?

conversations.title: Introducing yourself to new coworkers.
conversations.scene: On her first day, Nora introduces Maya to the team.

lines.text: Everyone, this is Maya. She's our new designer.
Hi, everyone. Nice to meet you.
Welcome, Maya! I work in marketing.
Nice to meet you. What do you do in marketing?
I write the texts for our websites.
You'll work together a lot.
Great. If I have questions, can I ask you?
Of course. My desk is next to the window.

conversations.title: Participating in a team meeting.
conversations.scene: In the weekly meeting, the manager asks about a new project.

lines.text: Let's start. Nora, how is the hotel project going?
Well. We showed the first designs to the client on Monday.
And what did they say?
They liked them. Maya, do you want to add something?
Yes. They want brighter colors. I'll send new versions on Thursday.
Good. Does anyone see any problems?
I think we need more photos. Can we book a photographer?
Good idea. Nora, can you organize that?
Sure. I'll find someone this week.
Great. Let's meet again next Monday.

conversations.title: Asking your manager to clarify a task.
conversations.scene: The manager gives Maya a new task, but some things are not clear.

lines.text: Maya, can you make a poster for the spring sale?
Of course. Can I ask a few questions first?
Sure.
What size should it be, and is it for print or online?
Both. A large one for the store, and one for social media.
Do you have the texts, or should I write them?
Marketing will send the texts.
And when do you need it?
Next Friday at the latest.
OK. So, two versions, texts from marketing, by Friday. Is that right?
Exactly. Thank you.

conversations.title: Explaining your work progress and difficulties.
conversations.scene: Nora asks Maya how the poster is going.

lines.text: How's the poster coming along?
It's going well. The design for the store is almost finished.
Great. And the online version?
That's the difficult part. The texts are too long for a phone screen.
Have you talked to marketing?
Yes, but they haven't answered yet.
I'll call them. You need the shorter texts by tomorrow.
That would help a lot. Then I can finish on Thursday.
Perfect. Show me the store version this afternoon.

conversations.title: Negotiating a deadline or asking for more time.
conversations.scene: Maya needs more time for a big project.

lines.text: Do you have a moment? It's about the hotel website.
Sure, Maya. Is there a problem?
The client sent new changes yesterday, so I can't finish by Friday.
How much more time do you need?
Could I have until next Wednesday?
Wednesday is difficult. The client wants it before the weekend.
Then I could send the main pages on Friday, and the rest on Wednesday.
That works. I'll tell the client.
Thank you for understanding.

conversations.title: Reporting a technical problem to IT support.
conversations.scene: Maya's laptop won't connect to the office network.

lines.text: IT support. What's the problem?
My laptop won't connect to the network.
Since when?
Since this morning. Everyone else is fine.
Have you tried restarting it?
Yes, twice. It still doesn't work.
Let me look. Ah, your password has expired.
Oh! How do I change it?
Click here and choose a new one. At least twelve characters.
Done. It works now. Thank you!

conversations.title: Giving and receiving constructive feedback.
conversations.scene: After a client presentation, Nora and Maya talk about how it went.

lines.text: Can I give you some feedback on the presentation?
Of course. Please be honest.
Your designs were excellent. The client loved the colors.
But you spoke very fast. Try to slow down and make pauses.
That's fair. I was nervous.
Can I give you some feedback too?
Sure.
You answered the questions really well, but the start was a bit long.
You're right. Next time, I'll keep it shorter. Thanks, Maya.

conversations.title: Requesting vacation or sick leave.
conversations.scene: Maya wants a week off when her parents visit, and today she feels sick.

lines.text: Can I talk to you about my vacation?
Of course. When would you like to go?
The last week of August. My parents are coming to visit.
Let me check the calendar. Nora is away then too.
I can finish the important projects before I leave.
OK, then it's fine. Please send me an email request.
I will. And one more thing: I feel sick today. Can I go home early?
Of course. If you're still sick tomorrow, call me and stay at home.
Thank you. I'll let you know.

conversations.title: Discussing salary, working hours, or contract conditions.
conversations.scene: After six months, Maya asks about her contract.

lines.text: Thank you for meeting me. I'd like to talk about my contract.
Of course. What would you like to discuss?
My trial period ends this month. I'd like to ask for a higher salary.
You've done very good work. What did you have in mind?
A 10 percent raise. I now lead two client projects.
I can offer 7 percent now, and we'll talk again in six months.
Could I also work from home one day a week?
Yes, that's possible.
Then 7 percent and one day at home is a deal.
Great. Human resources will send you the new contract.

conversations.title: Enrolling in a school or language course.
conversations.scene: Maya wants to sign up for an evening language course.

lines.text: Hello. I'd like to sign up for a language course.
Of course. What level are you?
I'm a beginner, maybe A1.
You can do a short test online, or start in the A1 class.
When are the classes?
Monday and Wednesday evenings, from 6 to 8.
How much does it cost?
280 euros for ten weeks. The books are included.
Great. Can I pay by card?
Yes. Please fill in this form first.

conversations.title: Introducing yourself to a teacher and classmates.
conversations.scene: It's Maya's first lesson, and the teacher asks everyone to introduce themselves.

lines.text: Welcome, everyone! Please tell us your name and where you're from.
Hi, I'm Yuki. I'm from Japan.
Hello, I'm Maya. I'm from Canada.
Welcome, Maya. Why are you learning the language?
I live here now. I want to talk to my neighbors.
Great reason! And you, Yuki?
I study photography here. I want to make friends.
Wonderful. Maya, you can sit next to Yuki.

conversations.title: Asking a question during a lesson.
conversations.scene: The teacher uses a word Maya doesn't know.

lines.text: Excuse me, I have a question.
Yes, Maya?
What does "neighborhood" mean?
It's the area where you live. The streets around your home.
Ah, I see. How do you spell it?
I'll write it on the board.
And can you say it again, please?
Neighborhood. Repeat after me.

conversations.title: Explaining that you don't understand an assignment.
conversations.scene: Yuki doesn't understand what to do for homework.

lines.text: Excuse me, I don't understand the homework.
No problem. Which part is unclear?
Exercise 3. Do we write a letter or an email?
An email, to a friend, about your weekend.
How long should it be?
About 100 words.
And when do we have to hand it in?
On Wednesday. You can send it to me by email.
OK, now I understand. Thank you!

conversations.title: Working with classmates on a group project.
conversations.scene: Yuki, Maya and another student plan a presentation about the city.

lines.text: So, we have to talk about the city's history for ten minutes.
Let's divide the work. Who wants to do what?
I can make the slides. I'm a designer.
I'll research the old town and the castle.
Then I'll take photos, and I'll write about the markets.
When shall we meet again?
How about Saturday morning, here in the library?
Saturday works for me. Let's share our notes online before then.
Good idea. I'll make a shared folder tonight.

conversations.title: Asking for help with homework.
conversations.scene: Timo is stuck on his homework, and Leon is busy cooking.

lines.text: Dad, can you help me with my homework?
I'm cooking, Timo. Ask Maya, she's good at math.
Maya, can you help me, please?
